title: 2008 AMC 12A Problem 12
statement: A function \(f\) has domain \([0, 2]\) and range \([0, 1].\) (The notation \([a, b]\) denotes \(\{x : a \le x \le b\}.\)) What are the domain and range, respectively, of the function \(g\) defined by \[g(x) = 1 - f(x + 1)?\]

solutions.text:
The value \(f(x + 1)\) is defined when \(0 \le x + 1 \le 2,\) that is, \(-1 \le x \le 1,\) so the domain of \(g\) is \([-1, 1].\)

As \(f(x + 1)\) ranges over \([0, 1],\) the value \(1 - f(x + 1)\) ranges over \([0, 1]\) as well, so the range of \(g\) is \([0, 1].\)

Thus, B is the correct answer.
hints: Subtracting \(f(x + 1) \in [0, 1]\) from \(1\) reverses the interval but keeps it \([0, 1]\)
